crime_highlights: Mr. Milne died approximately one hour later as a result of fourteen sharp-force injuries; ten were stab wounds, and four were cuts.
rationale_highlights: taking into account the individualized Gladue factors that affect the culpability of Ms. Florence
her father's exclusion from aboriginal status was one of two causes of his alcoholism
Ms. Florence witnessed her father's drinking and his abuse of her mother
She is affected by these systemic factors which provide a context for this sentencing.
note: Factors only 'context'; court never says they reduced culpability or sentence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Cote approached the car, swinging a heavy chain.
He smashed the rear passenger-side window, near where Mr. Thomson sat, with the chain and then leaned or reached into the vehicle to pepper spray Mr. Thomson.
He was struck almost immediately by a minivan.
He never regained consciousness and his medical condition slowly deteriorated over the next two weeks.
rationale_highlights: I am satisfied that the systemic factors that play a part in the over‑representation of aboriginal persons in our prison system have also played some role in now bringing him before this court
The second consideration relevant to the issue of moral blameworthiness in this case arises from the application of R. v. Gladue
the reality is that their constrained circumstances may diminish their moral culpability
The foregoing comments are relevant to Mr. Cote's circumstances and conduct.
note: Court applies Ipeelee diminished-culpability passage to Cote (para 74).

crime_highlights: She was stabbed in the heart by the accused.
rationale_highlights: The accused is a 50-year old Aboriginal person who is an Indian Residential School survivor.
His parents were also alcoholics. They were also Indian Residential School survivors.
Gerald lost the use of his language and will not speak his Secwepemc (Shuswap) language as a direct result of the physical punishment he received at the Kamloops Indian Residential School
I have to consider the accused's tragic Aboriginal background and the impact that background has had on his moral culpability for committing this offence.
I also have to ensure that the sentence that I impose on this accused does not lead inadvertently to discrimination in sentencing.
note: Background's impact on moral culpability; defence-sought 4y5m imposed vs Crown 6y.
